title: Last-entry marking preserves block length
statement: Fix a width $w$, and let $B = ((i_1,b_1),\dots,(i_k,b_k))$ be a finite list whose entries are pairs, each consisting of an index in $\{0,1,\dots,w-1\}$ together with a boolean. Form a new list of triples by appending to every entry a marker flag, set to true on the final entry of $B$ and to false on all earlier entries. Then this list of triples has the same length as $B$.
hypotheses_covered: B is an arbitrary finite list of index-boolean pairs of width w
